title: Quantum Statistical Thermal Engine at the BCS-BEC crossover
authors: Santiago Henríquez Lira, Felipe Isaule, Martín HvE Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Patricio Vargas, Thomás Fogarty
abstract: We propose a quantum heat engine based on a two-component Fermi gas with s-wave contact interaction, operating across the BCS-BEC crossover. The work is extracted from the statistical properties of the gas, which are controlled by the interaction, rather than relying solely on compression and expansion stages. Using the functional renormalization group formalism, we obtain the equation of state in a non-perturbative form along the crossover, encompassing the superfluid-normal phase transition. The cycle combines isentropic density strokes, isochoric thermalization, and isothermal interaction sweeps. This construction makes it possible to integrate features of both Otto and Carnot cycles, in which the system simultaneously saturates both efficiency limits without the net work vanishing. In the absence of density variations, the cycle reduces to a statistical Stirling-like engine, in which the work generated arises exclusively from the interaction, achieving efficiencies up to $38\%$. A pronounced asymmetry emerges through the crossover, giving rise to distinct operating regimes depending on the trajectory followed in the phase diagram. Consequently, the same architecture can be tuned to function as an engine, refrigerator, accelerator, or heater. These findings highlight pairing correlations as a versatile thermodynamic resource for quantum heat machines.
summary: This work develops a quantum heat engine model based on a Fermi gas undergoing the BCS-BEC crossover. By analyzing a specialized Statistical Thermal Cycle (STC) using the FRG formalism, the authors demonstrate that the engine's performance is dictated by the gas's quantum statistics, not just volume changes. This allows the system to function as a versatile machine with tunable efficiency.
main_problem: The paper proposes and analyzes a quantum heat engine that operates by exploiting the internal quantum statistical structure of the working medium across the BCS-BEC crossover.
main_result: The engine can function as a versatile machine (engine, refrigerator, accelerator, or heater) because the work extraction relies on the interaction-driven changes in the gas's statistical character, achieving efficiencies up to 38%.
method: The study employs the Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) formalism to derive the equation of state non-perturbatively, followed by the construction and analysis of a Statistical Thermal Cycle (STC).
model_or_system: The system is a three-dimensional Fermi gas with two spin components interacting via s-wave contact interactions, allowing tuning between BCS superfluid and BEC molecular regimes.
key_observables: Efficiency ($\eta_{ST}$), net work ($w_{net}$), heat flows ($q_H, q_L$), and the energy per particle ($e$).
important_parameters: Scattering length ($a$), density ($n$), temperature ($T$), and the dimensionless interaction parameter ($c_F = 1/(k_F a)$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a truncated ansatz within the FRG framework, and the cycle is analyzed by combining isentropic, isochoric, and isothermal statistical strokes.
figures_summary: Figures map the operational regimes (Engine, Refrigerator, Accelerator, Heater) across the BCS-BEC crossover and show the dependence of efficiency on interaction parameters.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using FRG to calculate thermodynamics across the crossover. It then details the construction of the six-stroke Statistical Thermal Cycle (STC) and analyzes how the work and heat are exchanged in each stroke, concluding with a comprehensive mapping of the machine's operational versatility.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, tunable model for quantum thermal machines, showing how fundamental many-body physics (BCS-BEC crossover) can be harnessed as a thermodynamic resource, which is highly relevant to quantum thermodynamics.
